about: Politician profiles. Each starts from a party snapshot of their era (base, base_year) and is adjusted where the person's own stated views differ: 'axes' shifts all facets of an axis, 'facets' sets a facet. Views only, not actions. Built into data/actors by tools/build_people.py.

notes.MIG: Leads the VVD's tougher line on asylum and migration.

people.name: Frans Timmermans
people.role: Former EU climate commissioner and GroenLinks-PvdA leader
people.label: GroenLinks-PvdA leader

notes.INT: Long-time EU insider, strongly pro-European.
notes.CLI: Architect of the European Green Deal.

notes.MIG: Migration was hardly a political divide in his time.
notes.CLI: Environment was an emerging concern, climate not yet.
notes.TEC: Broadly optimistic about planning and technology.

people.label: President

notes.ECO: Social democrat of the old school: unions and the eight-hour day.
notes.SOC: Measured against today's norms.
notes.LIB: Put down revolutionary uprisings to protect the new republic.
notes.MIG: Not an issue in his time.
notes.DEM: Chose parliamentary democracy over a council republic.

notes.ECO: Father of the social market economy: free prices, competition, 'Wohlstand für alle'.
notes.SOC: Values of the 1950s.
notes.MIG: Guest-worker era, not yet a divide.
notes.CLI: Not yet an issue.

people.name: Franz Josef Strauß
people.role: Leader of the CSU 1961 to 1988, Minister-President of Bavaria
people.label: Chancellor candidate

notes.SOC: Catholic conservative: 'right of the CSU there can be no democratic party'.
notes.LIB: Hard line on law and order in the 1970s.
notes.INT: Hawkish Cold Warrior, built up the Bundeswehr as defence minister.
notes.TEC: Champion of nuclear power and aerospace.
notes.CLI: Not yet a political issue.

notes.ECO: Ecological and anti-capitalist roots of the early Greens.
notes.DEM: 'Anti-party party': grassroots democracy against the establishment.
notes.TEC: Against nuclear power and nuclear weapons.
notes.INT: Pacifist, against NATO missiles.
notes.LIB: Human rights and nonviolence.

people.name: Joschka Fischer
people.role: Foreign minister and Vice Chancellor 1998 to 2005 (Greens)
people.label: Foreign minister

notes.ECO: Led the pragmatic 'Realo' wing.
notes.INT: Backed the Kosovo intervention ('never again Auschwitz') and a federal Europe.
notes.CLI: Climate policy was taking shape under red-green.

people.name: Markus Söder
people.role: Minister-President of Bavaria, leader of the CSU
people.label: Current

people.name: Lars Klingbeil
people.role: SPD co-leader, Vice Chancellor and finance minister
people.label: Current

notes.ECO: From the SPD's pragmatic centre.
notes.INT: Pushed the SPD towards higher defence spending.
'Feminist foreign policy' and strong support for arming Ukraine.

people.name: Hans-Georg Maaßen
people.role: Former head of the domestic intelligence service, leader of the WerteUnion
people.label: WerteUnion

notes.ECO: The 'People's Budget': taxes on land and the rich to pay for pensions and national insurance.
notes.DEM: Took on the House of Lords.

people.name: William Gladstone
people.role: Prime Minister four times between 1868 and 1894 (Liberal)
people.label: Midlothian campaign

notes.ECO: Free trade, low taxes and 'retrenchment' of public spending.
notes.SOC: Devout Anglican moralist.
notes.INT: Against imperial adventures; for Irish Home Rule.

notes.ECO: 'One Nation' Toryism: public health and factory acts for the working class.
notes.SOC: Church, Crown and traditional order.
notes.INT: Imperialist; made Victoria Empress of India.
notes.MIG: Not an issue in his time.

people.name: Ian Paisley
people.role: Founder of the DUP, First Minister of Northern Ireland 2007 to 2008
people.label: Against the Good Friday Agreement

notes.SOC: Free Presbyterian preacher and the loudest voice of 'Ulster says no'; deeply conservative on morals.
notes.DEM: Opposed the 1998 agreement, later shared power with Sinn Féin.

notes.ECO: 'Predistribution', energy price freezes and responsible capitalism.
notes.CLI: Wrote the Climate Change Act as minister in 2008; now drives clean power by 2030.
Slowed net zero measures such as the petrol car ban.
notes.TEC: Hosted the first AI Safety Summit, pro-innovation.

notes.INT: Lifelong campaigner for nuclear disarmament.

people.name: Alex Salmond
people.role: First Minister of Scotland 2007 to 2014, founder of Alba
people.label: Independence referendum

notes.ECO: Wanted low corporation tax for an independent Scotland, alongside free tuition.
notes.SOC: More traditional than the SNP after him.
notes.CLI: Backed renewables and North Sea oil alike.

notes.ECO: Public control of buses and rail, against austerity.
notes.DEM: 'King of the North': power to the regions, against Westminster centralism.

notes.SOC: Against the spread of slavery; later abolition through the Thirteenth Amendment.
notes.DEM: 'Government of the people, by the people, for the people.'
notes.ECO: Whig economics: tariffs, railways, homesteads.

people.name: Eugene V. Debs
people.role: Socialist Party presidential candidate, five times
people.label: 1912 campaign

notes.ECO: 'Extremism in the defense of liberty is no vice': small government and lower taxes.
notes.LIB: Libertarian streak; later backed gay service members.
notes.INT: Hard-line anti-communist.
notes.DEM: Against the Washington establishment of both parties.

notes.ECO: Accepted wage and price controls and a large federal role.
notes.CLI: Created the EPA and signed the Clean Air Act.
notes.LIB: Law and order and the 'silent majority'.
notes.INT: Détente with the Soviet Union and the opening to China.

people.name: George Wallace
people.role: Governor of Alabama, 1968 American Independent candidate
people.label: 1968 campaign

notes.ECO: Against corporate power and for consumer protection.
notes.SOC: Focused on economics more than culture.
notes.MIG: Less outspoken on immigration than today's Greens.

people.name: Hillary Clinton
people.role: Secretary of State 2009 to 2013, 2016 Democratic nominee
people.label: 2016 nominee

notes.ECO: Centrist economics with an expanded Affordable Care Act.
notes.INT: Interventionist on Libya and Syria.

notes.ECO: A wealth tax and tough regulation of Wall Street.
notes.TEC: Wants to break up big tech.
notes.DEM: Fights corporate influence in Washington.

notes.ECO: Business-minded fiscal conservative; built a health plan in Massachusetts.
notes.MIG: Spoke of 'self-deportation' in 2012.
notes.DEM: Institutionalist; later the only Republican senator to vote to convict Trump twice.

notes.ECO: More conventional small-government conservative than Trump.
notes.DEM: Works through state institutions; 'where woke goes to die'.

notes.ECO: Pragmatic centrist on the economy.
notes.TEC: Infrastructure, EVs and innovation.

people.name: Zohran Mamdani
people.role: Mayor of New York City (Democrat, DSA)
people.label: Mayor

notes.ECO: Democratic socialist: rent freezes, free buses, city-run grocery stores and higher taxes on the rich.
notes.MIG: Defends New York as a sanctuary city.
notes.DEM: Won against the party establishment.
notes.LIB: Wants to shift money from policing to public safety services.
notes.INT: Critical of US military aid to Israel.

notes.SOC: Openly gay, progressive on social questions.
notes.MIG: Wants to make legal immigration much easier.
